findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: During the inspection the facility was unable to provide Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificates for staff at the facility. The PIC contacted the primary manager for consultation. They could not find the certifications at the facility during the inspection. The inspectors will verify sufficient CFPMS at the next routine inspection. Ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs available to cover all shifted where foods are handled/prepared in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: During the inspection the facility was unable to provide verified and signed reporting agreements/documents from all staff. The PIC contacted the primary manager about this paperwork. However, they could not find it in the facility. The inspectors will verify all reporting agreements on next schedule follow up. Ensure that all reporting agreements should be available, signed, by all employees.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The inspectors observed significant soil on the blades of knives on the magnetic strip used for storing cleaned utensils that were ready for use. The PIC was made aware of it moved them to dish for re-cleaning.  Any food contact items should be cleaned and sanitized completely prior to storage and future use.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: During the inspection, inspectors observed that there was a gap underneath the back door with observable light coming through. This should be sealed so it protected against any type of pest/rodent entrance. Repaired prior to next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: The inspectors observed a pen and a lip balm in the pan along with empty oregano shakers on the prep-table. The PIC was notified and discarded the items to correct. The shakers were aLos moved to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces that make contact with ready to eat foods are protected from contamination from personal/ miscellaneous Items.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the ceiling piece of the microwave in the front of the facility was falling off. Repair prior to next routine inspection. Ensure that all physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: On arrival a personal drink was observed on the prep-table where foods were being actively portioned. The drink was moved to its appropriate designated location prior to notifying the PIC. Make sure that all personal items/food/drink should be separated from prep area, personal items can increase a risk of contamination of other food.
findings.citation_text: 403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Food Handler certificates were not able to be produced for all employees present at today’s inspection. To ensure safe food handling practices, all employees must obtain and be able to produce a Food Handler’s Card within 30 days of hire. Ensure all employees have their Food Handler’s Cards by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.[C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed hand washing sink to have no paper towels. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) replaced paper towels. Ensure all hand washing sinks have warm running water, soap, and paper towels at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There were no active Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPMs) present at today’s inspection. One employee had an expired CFPM, and no one else at the facility had taken the class. A CFPM must be present during all hours in which food is being prepared or handled. The inspector shared a list of approved CFPM courses to the person in charge (PIC). Ensure multiple employees obtain or renew their CFPMs to ensure the PIC has a wide breath of food safety knowledge they can share with other staff members.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no paper towels in the all gender restroom. CORRECTED- a staff member replaced the paper towels. Ensure all handwashing sinks are stocked with warm running water, soap, and paper towels to decrease the risk of food-borne illnesses.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket to have 50 ppm of quaternary ammonia at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the PIC remade the sanitizer to 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer buckets are changed (and checked with the facility’s test strips) at a frequency to maintain the proper sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: A knife in ready-to-use position (on the prep tables’s magnetic strip) was observed to contain an accumulation of food debris. CORRECTED- the knife was taken to the facility’s triple sink to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Multiple foods were observed to be above the accepted cold holding value of 41F (tomatoes- probed at 45.9F, red onions- probed at 46F, and cucumbers- probed at 46.4F, spinach- probed at 45.1) on the west prep line cooler during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that the items were prepared at the start of the day- over 4 hours ago. CORRECTED- the PIC voluntarily discarded the aforementioned ready to eat (RTE) food items. Close cooler lids when not in use, and routinely probe RTE items to ensure they are holding internal temperatures below 41F. RTE foods must not be left in the “Temperature Danger Zone” (41-135) for more than 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation of food debris during today’s inspection:
1) Food pan areas of prep coolers
2) Along the back hinges of the prep coolers
3) Under the cookie display box.
4) All interior walls of the microwave.
5) Magnetic knife strip over the kitchen prep table.
To prevent the contamination of RTE foods, nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of food debris. Encourage staff to clean during slower times when food preparation is not occurring.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Multiple areas in the physical facility were observed to be in need of repair:
1) The caulking along the triple sink was observed to be discolored and fragmented. The current caulking should be removed and replaced.
2) The caulking behind the meat slicer was incomplete. Complete caulking this area.
Counters, plumbing, and other items that are fixed in place (and cannot be moved for cleaning) should be sealed to the wall to prevent the harborage of mold, and provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Food Handler certificates were not able to be produced for all employees present at today’s inspection. To ensure safe food handling practices, all employees must obtain and be able to produce a Food Handler’s Card within 30 days of hire. Ensure all employees have their Food Handler’s Cards by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.[C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
An employee was observed moving from operating the cash register, donning gloves, and preparing a sandwich without washing hands. Hands must be washed after any task that may have contaminated their hands (such as operating the cash register), and before donning gloves. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Review when to wash hands with employees.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Sanitizer in the 3 compartment sink was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- PIC drained and refilled the sink with fresh sanitizer. Sanitizer was observed at 150ppm. Dishes in the rinse basin were re-sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label [150-400ppm], and water with 500ppm hardness or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
A container of banana peppers in the walk-in cooler was observed with a use-by date of 8/15 (inspection on 8/17). CORRECTED- Peppers were voluntarily discarded. Ensure foods are used or discarded within 7 days of preparation or before their use-by date.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Food debris and soil accumulation was observed around the top edges of the service prep coolers, in the gap between the soda machine and microwave cabinets, and on the front service area cabinet door pulls. Detail cleaning is needed in those locations.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Broken trim tile observed to the left of the triple sink, creating a gap along the floor/wall junction. Repair or replace broken tile.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
A mop bucket was observed near the mop sink containing a mop and dirty water. PIC indicated that mopping takes place at night. Ensure mop water is discarded after use and that mops are stored in a manner that promotes drying.
6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Corner trim is missing near the passage to the service counter near the handwashing sink, exposing the wall and the surface covering. In this area, the wall covering is warped out near the base trim, creating a gap. There is a gap between the two base trim tile pieces at the corner as well. Seal the corner so that the wall is protected and gaps are sealed.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand washing sink in the all-gender restroom has a paper towel dispenser which was stocked but not functioning correctly resulting in paper-towels not dispensing as required. Paper towels must be available at all times for each hand sink. Operator corrected the dispenser and paper towels were available during the inspection. Ensure that paper towel dispensers are not just stocked but are functioning properly to allow paper towels to be obtained following hand washing. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Soda nozzles were observed to be covered in black mold by checking with a clean paper towel. Soda nozzles are food-contact surfaces. Food-contact surfaces must be cleaned regularly to prevent the accumulation of residue, debris and mold. Ensure that soda nozzles are cleaned regularly and thoroughly the prevent buildup from occurring. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the meatballs at the front prep area were stored in a steam table at a temperature of 131 degrees F or lower. Facility temperature logs show that meatballs were checked this morning and were 160 degrees immediately after removing from the microwave. Checking the meatballs immediately after cooking is a great practice to ensure that meatballs are reaching the appropriate cooking temperature, however, ensure that temperatures are checked shortly after to ensure that hot-holding temperatures remain at-or-above 135 degrees throughout the course of service. Microwaves do not cook food evenly so time must be given to ensure that temperatures are allowed to stabilize before you take temperatures. Meatballs were immediately brought to 135 degrees by increasing the temperature of the steam table. Corrected on site.  

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a personal mobile phone sitting on a wire shelf directly above food preparation. Operator was removing the bag from a container of spinach immediately underneath the phone. Operator was told to cease food preparation immediately, do not remove the bag and expose the food, and remove the phone from the food preparation area. The phone was removed and hands were washed appropriately immediately after. Ensure that personal phones and other personal items which are sources of contamination are not ever stored above or in contact with food. Corrected on site. 

3-305.12: FOOD may not be stored: (A) In locker rooms; (B) In toilet rooms; (C) In dressing rooms; (D) In garbage rooms; (E) In mechanical rooms; (F) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (G) Under leaking water lines, including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads, or under lines on which water has condensed; (H) Under open stairwells; or (I) Under other sources of contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Several tiles throughout the facility are cracked and/or peeling from the wall. These areas include near the mop sink/rear door, near the soda boxes at the rear of the facility, and to the left of the triple sink along the floor/wall junction. Inspector also observed that caulking around the triple sink was missing in several areas and has deteriorated across the entire wall/equipment junction leaving a gap. Surfaces in food preparation areas or areas subject to moisture but be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that tiles in the kitchen are repaired/replaced as needed and that caulking around all sinks remains intact. Correct tile and caulking by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in a sani-bucket was observed at less than 100ppm quat, and solution at the 3 part sink was observed around 100ppm quat. Valves were changed resulting in concentrations that were above 400ppm. Putting the original valve on that allowed for proper concentration after corrective action was taken on 9/17/21 along with a new elbow connection allowed for sanitizer to dispense at proper concentration of 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration of sanitizer.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-201.11 Spray bottle of peroxide cleaner and disinfectant was hanging on the shelving above prep table in back where food prep was occurring. Spray bottle was moved to chemical storage area. Ensure proper storage of chemicals.
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles by separating toxic materials by spacing or partitioning and locating toxic materials in an area that is not above food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Upon arrival of inspector the PIC at the time of inspection was unsure as to where certifications were located to show proof of CFM. Staff were unaware that sanitizer dispenser was not functioning properly (see violation 16 for details). One employee went to put on gloves to do food prep without first washing hands, and employees were observed washing hands without proper technique (see violation 8 for details). Area manager arrived during inspection to locate certifications but did not currently have a copy of personal certification. Violations will be revisited at spot check in 10 days. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employees were observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed. Area manager was advised to revisit proper handwashing with all staff and ensure staff are properly washing hands. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee went to put on gloves for food prep without first washing their hands. Just prior to getting gloves the employee was observed going in and out of the walk-in cooler and adjusting their hair. Employee was advised on handwashing prior to glove use and washed hands before continuing with prep.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, prior to donning gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Freshly dispensed quat solution was observed at 100ppm. Area manager attempted an adjustment of water temperature to see if that was the issue. It appeared to help slightly, but the concentration was still negligible. Maintenance came to the facility during inspection and changed the valves in the dispenser. The concentration was observed at 200ppm after the valve was changed.  
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration of sanitizer.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 (E) Soda nozzle diffusers were observed with varying amounts to discoloration and buildup. Clean the soda nozzles and diffusers daily to eliminate buildup. Soaking alone will not remove buildup. Nozzles and diffusers also need to be cleaned and sanitized.
Equipment such as dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Bottles of milk in the lobby drink cooler had surface temperatures at 45F-47F. Two bottles were probed to check internal temperatures. Bottle from the back had an internal temperatures of 46F and the bottle from the front was observed at 45F. The drink cooler had a significant amount of ice buildup on the condenser, which was likely effecting the temperature. Remaining milk was relocated to the walk-in cooler. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sani-bucket had old solution in it from the evening prior. Sanitizer solution was not yet prepared for the current operating day. Sanitizer was provided during inspection. Ensure sani-bucket is prepared and sanitizer solution is available during all hours of prep and operation.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Walk-in cooler shelves were soiled with mold in some ares. Clean the walk-in cooler shelves as needed to eliminate buildup of mold and debris. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.116 Wet mop head was stored in the basin of the mopsink. Ensure proper storage of the mop and other cleaning tools between uses. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employee washed hands for less than 20 seconds prior to putting on gloves to prepare an order. Proper handwashing was discussed; employee was later observed washing hands for proper length of time. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towel dispenser in women's room was empty. Paper towels were provided during inspection. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution used for wiping knives between uses was observed at 0ppm quat. Solution was changed out during inspection. Ensure the knife sanitizing caddy is changed out frequently/as needed throughout the operating day and maintained at proper concentration of 150-400ppm as required per product label directions. 
--Sani-bucket by handsink was observed at 100ppm quat. Solution was prepared with hot water. Preparation of sanitizer solution with cool to warm water (65F-75F) was discussed. New solution was dispensed with warm instead of hot water and observed at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Steak was observed with surface and internal temperatures of 52F and 50F respectively. Per information provided by staff the steak was likely thawed in a pan of water within the last 2 hours prior to placing in the cold table for service. Pan of steak was placed in the freezer to help quickly drop temperature prior to placing back on the cold line for service. Proper thawing was also discussed.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 Manager was unsure where the thermocouple probe was located for the thermometer and was only using the infrared part of the thermometer for taking temperatures. Store owner was contacted about purchasing a new food thermometer and advised manager where to look to find the thermocouple probe at the store. Cleaning and maintenance of food probe were discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text:
3-302.12 Spray bottle had label indicating it contained vegetable oil. Manager noted vegetable oil is not used at the facility, and the bottle in question should contain water. Ensure spray bottles of water are properly labeled as to the contents. 
Except for containers holding food that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding food or food ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the food establishment shall be labeled with the common name of the food.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Slider rolls in the freezer were observed in a carry out Subway bag. Although the bag is a single service article, it is not intended for storage of unpackaged foods. Rolls were placed in a food pan for proper storage. 
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-603.16 Employee washed a pan and placed it directly in the third compartment of 3 part sink that was in the process of filling with sanitizer. Employee was advised on proper rinsing between the wash and sanitize steps during ware washing. Pan was placed in middle compartment to be rinsed prior to sanitizing. Manager was advised to go over proper manual ware washing steps with staff
Washed utensils and equipment shall be rinsed so that abrasives are removed and cleaning chemicals are removed or diluted through the use of water by using a distinct, separate water rinse after washing and before sanitizing in the 3 compartment sink.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) counter soda machine on make line (dust and general debris);
B) upper compartment of dry storage cooler (food crumbs); and
C) Surfaces under/around equipment at lobby drink counter (splash/buildup).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11 Women's room handsink was loose from the wall. Re-seal the handsink to the wall in the women's room.
--Corner piece of ceramic baseboard was loose behind the chip rack. Repair the loose piece of baseboard. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.116 Damp mop head was stored in the basin of the mopsink. Mop head was positioned over the edge of the mopsink basin to allow for proper drying. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.
